mainTopic: The size of a כזית, the story of בר קפרא's students, and the ברכות on cooked vegetables, their water, dill, and soaked bread
overview: This amud opens by finishing a question. רבי יוחנן said a ברכה אחרונה on a pitted olive, which seems smaller than a כזית. The answer is that a כזית is measured by a medium olive, and his large olive stayed above that size even without its pit. A משנה confirms this, and רבי אבהו explains the olive's name. The גמרא then tries to show that the dispute over the ברכה on cooked vegetables goes back to the תנאים, using a story about two students before בר קפרא. It rejects that proof: the students may only have argued about which food comes first. Next come rulings on cut turnips and on vegetable dishes with flour, a side note about the health benefits of beets, and רב פפא's rule that cooking water gets the vegetable's ברכה. A משנה about dill shows that dill is added for flavor, which answers רב פפא's question. Finally, רב חייא בר אשי rules that soaked dry bread gets המוציא, and רבא challenges the claim that רבי חייא disagrees. The discussion of רבא's challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The pitted olive seems too small
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: a pitted olive is less than the required minimum size, so how could רבי יוחנן say a ברכה אחרונה on it?
steps.simpleTranslation: [How could רבי יוחנן say a blessing after eating it?] It is missing the required amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that started on the previous amud. It asks how רבי יוחנן could say a ברכה אחרונה on an olive whose pit had been removed, since what was left seems smaller than a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה אחרונה is only said after eating at least a כזית. An olive minus its pit should be smaller than a whole olive, so it seems to fall below that minimum. This makes רבי יוחנן's action look like a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The required halachic amount or minimum size
An olive-sized amount, the minimum for a ברכה אחרונה

phrases.english: It is lacking the required amount!
phrases.notes: This is the end of a question that began on the previous amud. The olive had its pit removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge to רבי יוחנן's behavior that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן saying a ברכה אחרונה on a pitted olive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה אחרונה needs a כזית. An olive without its pit is less than an olive, so it should not require one.

steps.title: The measure is a medium olive, and his olive was large
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a כזית is measured by a medium olive. רבי יוחנן's olive was large, so even without its pit it still reached that size.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think we need the size of a large olive? We only need the size of a medium olive, and that much was there. The olive brought before רבי יוחנן was a large one, so even though they took out its pit, the required amount was still left.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains that the questioner had the wrong idea about which olive sets the standard. A כזית means a medium olive, and רבי יוחנן's olive was big.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that a כזית means the size of whatever olive you are holding, or of a large olive. The answer sets a fixed standard: a medium olive. A large olive with its pit removed can still be as big as a medium whole olive, so רבי יוחנן ate the full amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? Used to point out a wrong assumption
Pit or stone of a fruit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer changes the rule that a ברכה אחרונה requires a כזית. That rule stays. The answer only clarifies which olive sets the size: a medium one.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
that we require the size of a large olive?
We require the size of a medium olive
(and that much was there),
and the one that they brought before רבי יוחנן
was a large olive,
so even though they removed its pit,
the required amount still remained.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ כְּזַיִת גָּדוֹל בָּעֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the questioner's assumption about the standard and clarifies the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כזית is measured by a large olive, or by the actual olive being eaten, so a pitted olive falls short.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כזית is measured by a medium olive. A large olive without its pit can still reach that size.

steps.title: A משנה proves the standard is a medium olive
steps.stepSummary: A משנה states that the olive used for halachic measures is neither small nor large but medium, called אגורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The olive that the חכמים spoke about is not small and not large, but medium, and that is the אגורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up the claim from Step 2 that a כזית is measured by a medium olive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 2 could have looked like a guess. This משנה shows that the medium-olive standard is an established rule from the חכמים. It also names the specific type of olive: the אגורי.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The name given to the medium olive variety

phrases.english: As we learned: The olive that they spoke of

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָטָן וְלֹא גָּדוֹל, אֶלָּא בֵּינוֹנִי —
phrases.english: is not small and not large, but medium —
and that is the 'אגורי.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: זַיִת שֶׁאָמְרוּ לֹא קָטָן וְלֹא גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the halachic כזית is measured by a medium olive
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה stating that the olive the חכמים meant is neither small nor large but medium, the אגורי

steps.title: רבי אבהו explains the name אגורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the olive's real name is אברוטי, or some say סמרוסי. It is called אגורי because its oil is stored up inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: Its name is not 'אגורי.' Its name is 'אברוטי,' and some say its name is 'סמרוסי.' So why is it called 'אגורי'? Because its oil is gathered up (אגור) inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds a side explanation about the word used in the משנה. He says אגורי is a description, not the olive's actual name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה itself does not change here. רבי אבהו only clarifies the word: the variety is really called אברוטי (or סמרוסי). The משנה calls it אגורי because the word comes from 'gathered,' describing how much oil the olive holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The real name of the olive variety, according to רבי אבהו
And some say (introducing a different version)
An alternate name for the olive

steps.whatToRemember: The halachic כזית is the size of a medium olive, the אגורי. That is why a large olive can still be a כזית even after its pit is removed.

phrases.english: And רבי אבהו said: Its name is not 'אגורי'
rather, its name is 'אברוטי,'
and some say its name is 'סמרוסי.'
And why is it called 'אגורי'?
Because its oil is gathered inside it.
phrases.notes: This is wordplay: אגורי sounds like אגור, meaning 'gathered.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: לֹא אֵגוֹרִי שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word that appeared in the משנה quoted in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The medium olive is really named אברוטי or סמרוסי. It is called אגורי because its oil is stored inside it.

steps.title: Proposing that the dispute goes back to the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the earlier argument about the ברכה on cooked vegetables is like a dispute among תנאים, and starts a story: two students sat before בר קפרא, and cabbage, plums, and pullets were brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute between תנאים: There were two students sitting before בר קפרא. They brought before him cabbage, Damascus plums, and pullets.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא proposes that an earlier argument matches an older dispute, and it begins a story that will show that dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase נימא כתנאי means 'let us say this follows a dispute of תנאים.' The argument being linked is whether cooked vegetables get בורא פרי האדמה or שהכל. The story sets the scene with three foods: two cooked plant foods and one meat dish. The order of their ברכות is what the story turns on.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: נימא is only a suggestion. The גמרא often proposes a link like this and then rejects it, so do not treat it as settled yet.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tannaim:
For there were two students
who were sitting before Bar Kappara.
They brought before him cabbage, Damascus plums, and pullets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to the earlier argument about cooked vegetables.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument over the ברכה on cooked vegetables parallels a dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the two students before בר קפרא

steps.title: A student blesses the pullets first and is mocked
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא lets one student make the ברכה. He rushes to bless the pullets, and his friend makes fun of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא gave one of them permission to make the blessing. He jumped and made the blessing over the pullets. His friend made fun of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. One student chooses to make the ברכה over the meat first, and the other student mocks that choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blessing the pullets first means he said שהכל and did not start with the plant foods. The friend mocks him, as if he grabbed the meat out of hunger or got the order wrong. The גמרא will soon explain what each student held about cooked vegetables.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara gave permission
to one of them to recite the blessing,
he jumped and blessed over the pullets.
His friend ridiculed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן בַּר קַפָּרָא רְשׁוּת לְאֶחָד מֵהֶן לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One student blessed the meat first, and the other mocked him for it.

steps.title: בר קפרא is first angry at the mocker
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא says he is angry at the student who mocked, not the one who blessed. Even if the blesser acted like someone who had never tasted meat, that is no reason to mock him.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא became angry and said: I am not angry at the one who made the blessing. I am angry at the one who made fun. Even if your friend acts like someone who never tasted meat in his life, why did you make fun of him?
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא first scolds the student who mocked. He says that even if the blesser grabbed the meat out of hunger, mocking him was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא is not yet ruling on which ברכה should come first. He objects to the way the second student behaved. Making fun of a friend is wrong no matter what the friend did.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who made the blessing

phrases.english: Bar Kappara became angry and said:
It is not at the one who blessed that I am angry,
rather, at the one who ridiculed I am angry.
If your friend is like

phrases.aramaic: כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא טָעַם טַעַם בָּשָׂר מֵעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: one who never tasted the taste of meat,
why did you ridicule him?

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּעַס בַּר קַפָּרָא אָמַר: לֹא עַל הַמְבָרֵךְ אֲנִי כּוֹעֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בר קפרא reacts to the mocking described in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mocking a friend is wrong, even if the friend seems to have acted out of hunger.

steps.title: בר קפרא turns his anger to the one who blessed
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא then says he is really angry at the one who blessed. If the student was unsure of the order, he should have asked the elder sitting in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said again: I am not angry at the one who made fun. I am angry at the one who made the blessing. And he said: Even if there is no wisdom here, is there no elder here?!
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא now turns to the student who made the ברכה. He scolds him for deciding the order of ברכות on his own instead of asking בר קפרא, the elder present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the blesser was not exactly his choice. It was that he did not consult the elder, which was disrespectful when unsure. So both students acted wrongly: one mocked, and the other did not ask. Steps 10 and 11 explain the legal dispute behind their behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and said, reconsidered

steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא was upset with both students: with the mocker for making fun of his friend, and with the blesser for not asking the elder. The גמרא will next use this story to show a dispute about cooked vegetables.

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְאָמַר: לֹא עַל הַמְלַגְלֵג אֲנִי כּוֹעֵס,
phrases.english: He went back and said: It is not at the one who ridiculed that I am angry,
rather, at the one who blessed I am angry.
And he said: If there is no wisdom here,
is there no elder here?!
phrases.notes: Meaning: if you were not sure, you should have asked me, the elder present.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְאָמַר: לֹא עַל הַמְלַגְלֵג אֲנִי כּוֹעֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the direction of בר קפרא's anger from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone unsure about the order of ברכות should ask the elder present rather than decide on his own.

steps.title: Both students died within the year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא ends the story: because of בר קפרא's anger, both students died before the year was over.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And neither of them lived out his year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story of בר קפרא and his two students. It tells us how it ended: both students died that year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא was angry at both of them, at the one who mocked and at the one who did not ask. This line shows how serious that anger was. It also closes the story so the גמרא can now ask what the story teaches about the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a teaching from the time of the תנאים)
They did not finish their year (they died within the year)

phrases.english: It was taught: And both of them did not live out their year.
phrases.notes: Both students died within that year because of בר קפרא's anger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in steps 5-8 by telling what happened to both students.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story ends with both students dying within the year. This shows how serious it was to mock a friend and to skip asking the elder who was present.

steps.title: Reading the story as a dispute about the ברכה on cooked vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two students disagreed about the ברכה on שלקות. The one who made the ברכה held that both foods are שהכל, so the food he likes better comes first. The one who mocked held that cooked vegetables are בורא פרי האדמה, so they come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they were arguing about? The one who made the ברכה held that cooked vegetables and pullets are both 'שהכל נהיה בדברו', so the food a person likes more comes first. The one who mocked held that cooked vegetables are 'בורא פרי האדמה' and pullets are 'שהכל', so the produce comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the story as proof that the earlier argument about cooked vegetables was already a dispute among תנאים. It explains each student's behavior through a different view of the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both foods have the same ברכה (שהכל), you start with the one you like more. That explains rushing to the pullets. If the vegetables are בורא פרי האדמה, their ברכה is more specific and more important, so they should go first. That explains why the friend mocked him.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that? (introduces a suggested reading)
The food a person likes more comes first
The produce (with the more specific ברכה) comes first

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'פירא' does not mean a tree fruit. It means the cooked vegetables, whose ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה, a more specific ברכה than שהכל.

phrases.english: Isn't it that they disagree about this:
phrases.notes: The גמרא proposes a reading of the story.

phrases.english: the one who made the blessing holds
phrases.notes: This is the student who rushed to bless the pullets.

phrases.english: that over cooked vegetables and pullets one says 'By whose word all things came to be,'
phrases.notes: Same ברכה for both foods.

phrases.english: therefore the food he prefers comes first;
phrases.notes: With equal ברכות, personal preference decides.

phrases.english: and the one who mocked holds that over cooked vegetables one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
and over pullets one says 'By whose word all things came to be,'
therefore the produce comes first.
phrases.notes: The more specific ברכה takes priority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the story is finished, the גמרא returns to the purpose announced in step 5: showing the dispute is like a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute about the ברכה on שלקות was already argued among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The behavior of בר קפרא's two students: one blessed the pullets first, the other mocked him

steps.title: Rejection: they agreed on the ברכה but argued about which food comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Both students may agree that both foods are שהכל. They argued only about priority: the food you like more, or cabbage because it nourishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that cooked vegetables and pullets are both 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'. Here they argue about a different idea. One holds that the food a person likes more comes first. The other holds that cabbage comes first, because it nourishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 10. It shows the story can be explained without any dispute about the ברכה on cooked vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students did not have to disagree about which ברכה cooked vegetables get. They could agree both foods are שהכל and still argue about which to bless first. One goes by personal preference, the other by nourishment. So the story does not prove a dispute among תנאים about שלקות.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of בר קפרא's students does not prove the ברכה on cooked vegetables. They may have agreed on שהכל for both foods and argued only about whether preference or nourishment decides which comes first.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
phrases.notes: The rejection begins.

phrases.english: that over cooked vegetables and pullets one says 'By whose word all things came to be,'
and here they argue about this reasoning:
phrases.notes: The dispute moves from the ברכה to the order of ברכות.

phrases.english: one Sage holds the preferred food comes first,
phrases.notes: The one who blessed the pullets.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds cabbage comes first, because it nourishes.
phrases.notes: The one who mocked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It does not decide the ברכה on שלקות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story can be explained by a different dispute (preference versus nourishment) while both sides agree on the ברכה.

steps.title: רב הונא: the ברכה on turnips depends on the size of the cut
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that רב הונא taught: turnip heads cut into large pieces get בורא פרי האדמה, and cut into small pieces they get שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: When we were in רב הונא's study hall, he told us: These turnip heads, if one cut them into large pieces, the ברכה is 'בורא פרי האדמה'. If one cut them into small pieces, it is 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new related topic: how the way a vegetable is prepared affects its ברכה. רבי זירא tells us what רב הונא taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that cutting the turnip into small pieces changes it enough that it loses its ברכה as produce and drops to שהכל. Large pieces still look like the vegetable, so they keep בורא פרי האדמה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב הוּנָא אֲמַר לַן:
phrases.english: When we were in the study hall of Rav Huna, he said to us:
These turnip heads:
if one cut them into large pieces, one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground';
phrases.notes: The vegetable is still recognizable.

phrases.english: if into small pieces, one says 'By whose word all things came to be.'
phrases.notes: The cutting changed it too much.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב הוּנָא אֲמַר לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and opens a new related discussion about how preparation affects a vegetable's ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turnips cut into large pieces get בורא פרי האדמה. Cut into small pieces, they get שהכל.

steps.title: רב יהודה: turnips are always בורא פרי האדמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that רב יהודה disagreed: large or small pieces, the ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה. Cutting them small is done only to make them taste sweeter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when we came to רב יהודה's study hall, he told us: Both large and small pieces get 'בורא פרי האדמה'. The reason a person cuts them up more is so that the taste becomes sweeter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא now gives a second ruling, from רב יהודה, which disagrees with רב הונא. For רב יהודה, cutting the turnip small does not change its ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה explains why the size does not matter. People cut turnips small to improve the flavor, not to ruin the vegetable. Since the cutting improves the turnip, it keeps its ברכה as produce, בורא פרי האדמה.

keyTerms.meaning: So that its taste becomes sweeter

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: large pieces of turnip get בורא פרי האדמה and small pieces get שהכל. רב יהודה: both get בורא פרי האדמה, because cutting small only improves the taste.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אֲתָאן לְבֵי רַב יְהוּדָה אֲמַר לַן:
phrases.english: And when we came to the study hall of Rav Yehuda, he said to us:
For both these and those, one says 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
phrases.notes: Large and small pieces alike.

phrases.english: and the fact that one cut them up more
is so that its taste becomes sweeter.
phrases.notes: The cutting improves the turnip, so it keeps its ברכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֲתָאן לְבֵי רַב יְהוּדָה אֲמַר לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second ruling that disagrees with רב הונא's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turnips get בורא פרי האדמה whether cut large or small, since cutting them small only sweetens their taste.

steps.title: רב כהנא's first ruling on beet and turnip dishes with flour
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב כהנא taught: a beet dish with little flour gets בורא פרי האדמה, but a turnip dish with a lot of flour gets בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in רב כהנא's study hall, he told us: A cooked beet dish, where people do not add much flour, gets 'בורא פרי האדמה'. A turnip dish, where people add a lot of flour, gets 'בורא מיני מזונות'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells us a ruling he heard from his teacher רב כהנא about which ברכה to say on cooked vegetable dishes that have flour mixed in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of flour seems to decide the ברכה. With little flour, the vegetable is the main food, so it is בורא פרי האדמה. With a lot of flour, the flour seems to become the main food, so the ברכה becomes בורא מיני מזונות.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה for grain-based foods: 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'

steps.confusionAlert: This is only רב כהנא's FIRST ruling. In the very next step he changes his mind, so do not treat this as the final הלכה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said,
when we were in the study hall of Rav Kahana
he said to us:
A cooked dish of beets,
to which they do not add much flour —
'Who creates fruit of the ground.'
A dish of turnips, to which they add more flour —
phrases.notes: תבשילא is understood here as well: 'a cooked dish of turnips'.

phrases.english: 'Who creates kinds of nourishment.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא אֲמַר לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of ברכות on cooked vegetables (like the turnip ruling of רב הונא and רב יהודה), now adding the question of flour mixed in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beet dish with little flour: בורא פרי האדמה. Turnip dish with much flour: בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: רב כהנא changes his mind: both dishes are בורא פרי האדמה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא retracts and rules that both beet and turnip dishes get בורא פרי האדמה, since the extra flour is only added to make the dish stick together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he changed his mind and said: Both of them get 'בורא פרי האדמה'. The extra flour that people throw into the turnip dish is only added to make it stick together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא takes back his first ruling and says both dishes get בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is the PURPOSE of the flour. The flour in the turnip dish is not there to be eaten as food in its own right; it is only a binder to hold the dish together. So the turnip stays the main food, and the ברכה follows the turnip.

keyTerms.meaning: And he went back and said (he changed his mind)
This and that; both of them

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה follows the main food. An ingredient added only to help the dish (like flour as a binder) does not change the ברכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a principle used throughout this sugya: we look at WHY an ingredient is added. The same question returns with the dill water later here.

phrases.english: And he went back and said:
Both this and that: 'Who creates fruit of the ground,'
and the fact that they throw more flour into it —
they do it merely to make it stick together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retracts the first ruling of step 14 about the turnip dish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both beet and turnip dishes get בורא פרי האדמה; flour added only as a binder does not change the ברכה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a beet dish is healthy
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a cooked beet dish is good for the heart, the eyes, and especially the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A cooked dish of beets is good for the heart, good for the eyes, and even more so for the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just mentioned a beet dish, it adds a side teaching from רב חסדא about the health benefits of beets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a הלכה about ברכות; it is health advice connected to the same food. The גמרא often brings related teachings once a topic comes up.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A cooked dish of beets
is good for the heart and good for the eyes,
and all the more so for the intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching triggered by the mention of a beet dish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cooked beet dish is healthy for the heart, eyes, and especially the intestines.

steps.title: אביי: only when it is cooked well
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the beet dish is only healthy when it sits on the stove and bubbles ('tukh tukh').
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is only true when the dish sits on the stove and goes 'tukh tukh' (bubbles and boils well).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a condition to רב חסדא's health teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's statement sounded general. אביי limits it: the benefit only comes when the beets are cooked thoroughly until the pot bubbles.

keyTerms.meaning: The bubbling sound of a boiling pot

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And that is when it sits on the stove
and makes 'tukh tukh' (bubbles).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְהוּא דְּיָתֵיב אַבֵּי תָפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition limiting רב חסדא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beet dish is only beneficial when it is boiled thoroughly.

steps.title: רב פפא: vegetable water has the same ברכה as the vegetable
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says it is obvious to him that water in which a vegetable was cooked has the same ברכה as the vegetable itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is obvious to me that beet water is like beets, turnip water is like turnips, and the water of any cooked vegetable is like that cooked vegetable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to ברכות. רב פפא gives a simple rule about the cooking water of vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water absorbs the taste of the vegetable, so it is treated like the vegetable. Whatever ברכה the vegetable gets (usually בורא פרי האדמה), its water gets the same.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
beet water is like beets,
and turnip water is like turnips,
and the water of all cooked vegetables is like all cooked vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the health side-topic to the laws of ברכות on cooked vegetables.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cooking water of a vegetable gets the same ברכה as the vegetable.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about dill water
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks what the ברכה is on dill water: is dill put in the pot to add flavor, or only to remove the scum?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: What about dill water? Do people put dill in to sweeten the taste, or do they put it in to remove the scum?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a question he is unsure about: the ברכה on water in which dill was cooked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the rule from רב כהנא, the answer depends on PURPOSE. If dill is added for flavor, it is a real food and its water is like vegetable water. If it is only added to clean out the scum, it is not being used as food, and its water would not get the vegetable's ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he could not resolve)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
What about dill water?
Do they use it to sweeten the taste,
or do they use it to remove the scum?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After stating the clear cases, רב פפא asks about an unclear case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is dill added to the pot for flavor (making its water like vegetable water) or only to remove scum (so it is not food)?

steps.title: Proof from the law of dill and תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: once dill has given its flavor in the pot, it no longer has the status of תרומה or of food for טומאה. This shows dill is used for flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Dill, once it has given its taste in the pot, no longer has the status of תרומה, and it can no longer become impure with food-impurity. Learn from this that people use dill to sweeten the taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's question by bringing a source about dill from the laws of תרומה and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says dill loses its food status only AFTER it gives its flavor. That means its whole value as food is the flavor it gives. So dill is put in the pot for taste, not just to remove scum, and dill water is like other vegetable water.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source to answer a question)
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן
The impurity that applies to food

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about ברכות directly. It comes from the laws of תרומה, and we learn from them what dill is used for.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Dill, once it has given taste in the pot,
no longer has the status of terumah,
and it does not become impure with food-impurity.
Learn from this
that they use it to sweeten the taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַשֶּׁבֶת מִשֶּׁנָּתְנָה טַעַם בַּקְּדֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That dill is added to the pot to give flavor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (in עוקצין) that dill loses תרומה and food-impurity status once it has given its taste in the pot.

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: yes, learn from this that dill is used for flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms that the proof works and closes רב פפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since dill is used for flavor, it counts as a real cooked vegetable. So dill water gets the same ברכה as other vegetable water.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה depends on why an ingredient is used: flour as a binder does not change the ברכה, and dill used for flavor makes its water like vegetable water.

phrases.english: Learn from this (yes, it is so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof from step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Dill is put in for flavor, so dill water gets the same ברכה as other cooked-vegetable water.

steps.title: Soaked dry bread still gets the ברכה of bread
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי rules that dry bread soaked in a bowl gets the ברכה of המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said: over dry bread that is soaking in a bowl, we say the ברכה of המוציא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב חייא בר אשי. Dry bread pieces that are soaking in a bowl still count as real bread for the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think soaking turns the bread into a different kind of food with a lower ברכה. רב חייא בר אשי says it is still פת and gets המוציא. The pieces are already broken, though, and that detail matters for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry pieces of bread, here soaked in a bowl

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said:
Dry bread soaking in a bowl
We recite over it "Who brings forth."
phrases.notes: It keeps the full status of bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. The גמרא moves from cooked vegetables to bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soaked dry bread pieces get המוציא.

steps.title: This ruling seems to argue with רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב חייא בר אשי's ruling seems to argue with רבי חייא, who says the ברכה must end together with the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי חייא. רבי חייא said that the ברכה must finish together with the breaking of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ruling just stated seems to clash with a rule of רבי חייא. This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא holds that the ברכה must finish just as the loaf is being broken. The bread is still connected when the ברכה begins. Soaked pieces are already broken off, so by רבי חייא's rule they would seem not to qualify for המוציא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names. רב חייא בר אשי gave the ruling about soaked bread. רבי חייא (no 'בר אשי') is a different, earlier sage whose rule seems to argue with it.

phrases.english: And this argues with Rabbi Chiyya,
For Rabbi Chiyya said:
The blessing must finish together with the bread [being broken].
phrases.notes: The ברכה should be completed while the bread is still being broken from the loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies a source that appears to contradict the ruling in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא: the ברכה must finish together with the breaking of the bread. This seems to exclude already broken pieces.

steps.title: רבא asks why already broken pieces should be any different
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the idea that רבי חייא disagrees. Even with a whole loaf, the ברכה finishes on a piece that has been cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Why should soaked bread be different? Is it because when the ברכה finishes, it finishes on a piece? With a whole loaf too, when the ברכה finishes, it finishes on a piece!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reasoning that soaked bread fails רבי חייא's rule because it is only a piece. He points out that a whole loaf also ends up as a piece by the time the ברכה is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason was that soaked bread is already a separate piece. But people usually cut into the loaf before the ברכה, so the ברכה on a whole loaf also ends on a piece. Therefore 'being a piece' cannot be the problem, and רבי חייא's rule must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A slice or piece of bread

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's challenge forces a new understanding of רבי חייא's rule about when to break bread. That understanding shapes the practice of how we cut bread around המוציא.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to it:
What is different about soaked bread, that one does not [say המוציא],
Because when the blessing finishes —
It finishes on a slice?
On a whole loaf too,
When he finishes it —
He finishes on a slice!
phrases.notes: Because one cuts into the bread before the ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 23 that רבי חייא's rule excludes soaked pieces.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumed reason that רבי חייא would exclude soaked bread because it is only a piece
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A whole loaf is also cut before the ברכה ends, so it too ends on a piece. Being a piece cannot be what disqualifies soaked bread.
